guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (asynchronous reset), err_q is driven to 0.
On positive edge of clk_i when rst_ni is high, if intg_err or reg_we_err is high, err_q is driven to 1.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i and rst_ni and (intg_err || reg_we_err)

guarantees.claim: On positive edge of clk_i when rst_ni is high, if neither intg_err nor reg_we_err is high, err_q retains its previous value.
guarantees.cond: posedge clk_i and rst_ni and !(intg_err || reg_we_err)

assumptions.claim: The system must assert rst_ni (async reset) to clear err_q back to 0 after an error condition has been handled, because err_q has no local clear mechanism.
assumptions.cond: After err_q has been set to 1
assumptions.risk: err_q remains high indefinitely, causing permanent error status and potentially preventing detection of new errors.

assumptions.claim: intg_err and reg_we_err must be stable at the rising edge of clk_i to ensure correct sampling.
assumptions.risk: Metastability or a missed pulse could cause err_q to not reflect the actual error, leading to silent error masking.

uncertain_points.claim: err_q is a sticky error flag with no clear mechanism other than reset. It is unclear if this behavior is intended or if a software-clearable bit should exist.
uncertain_points.risk: If software expects to clear the flag after handling an error but cannot, the flag may remain high and cause confusion or incorrect error reporting.
